challenges.title: Does data augmentation improve image classifier accuracy?
challenges.description: You want to test whether applying standard data augmentation (random flips, crops, colour jitter) during training increases the test accuracy of a CNN image classifier on a fixed dataset.
hints: You are turning augmentation on vs off — you control that directly. What method does that imply?
Test accuracy (%) is a number you measure. What data collection tool fits a numerical measurement?
Control for: model architecture, optimizer, learning rate, number of epochs, and random seed.

challenges.title: Does learning rate affect neural network training convergence speed?
challenges.description: You hypothesise that a higher learning rate causes a neural network to converge faster but with lower final accuracy. Design a study to test this across a range of learning rate values.
hints: You set the learning rate — you are directly manipulating it. Lab experiment.
Epochs-to-convergence and final validation loss are numerical measurements.
Control for: network architecture, dataset, batch size, weight initialisation, and random seed.

challenges.title: Does batch size affect model generalisation in deep learning?
challenges.description: There is evidence that large-batch training produces models that generalise worse than small-batch training (the 'sharp minima' hypothesis). Design a study to rigorously test this across multiple architectures.
hints: You manipulate batch size across multiple controlled runs — what method is this?
Measure both train/test accuracy gap and sharpness metrics — all quantitative.
Control for: total compute budget (not epochs), learning rate scaling rule, architecture, and dataset.

challenges.title: Does post-training quantization degrade LLM benchmark accuracy?
challenges.description: You want to measure how different quantization schemes (INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ) affect the downstream task accuracy of a large language model relative to its full-precision baseline.
hints: You apply different quantization schemes to the same base model — lab experiment with multiple conditions.
Benchmark scores (MMLU %, HellaSwag %, etc.) are quantitative measurements.
Control for: base model weights, evaluation prompts, temperature (set to 0), and hardware.

challenges.title: Which feature selection method maximises anomaly detection F1 in network traffic data?
challenges.description: You are comparing three feature selection approaches (mutual information, LASSO regularisation, and PCA) on their ability to improve the F1 score of an anomaly detector trained on high-dimensional network traffic logs.
hints: You are comparing THREE feature selection methods — which statistical test compares more than two group means?
F1 score per method is a numerical measurement. Run each method on identical train/test splits.
Control for: base classifier, dataset, train/test split seed, and class imbalance handling.

challenges.title: How does reward shaping strategy affect RL agent sample efficiency?
challenges.description: You want to understand how different reward shaping strategies (sparse, dense, potential-based) affect how quickly a reinforcement learning agent reaches a target performance threshold in a continuous control task.
hints: You control the reward function — manipulating it across conditions is a lab experiment.
Steps-to-threshold and final episodic return are quantitative. Average over many seeds.
Control for: policy architecture, optimiser, environment dynamics, episode length, and entropy coefficient.

challenges.title: Does LoRA rank affect catastrophic forgetting during LLM fine-tuning?
challenges.description: You want to model the relationship between LoRA adapter rank and the degree of forgetting on general-purpose benchmarks after fine-tuning a foundation model on a domain-specific task.
hints: You want to PREDICT forgetting from LoRA rank — which analysis method models a continuous predictor and outcome?
Measure forgetting as the delta in benchmark score (pre minus post fine-tuning) — quantitative.
Control for: base model, fine-tuning dataset, number of training steps, learning rate, and target modules.

challenges.title: What factors predict alignment quality in RLHF-trained language models?
challenges.description: You want to identify which preference data properties (annotator agreement rate, dataset size, domain diversity) and training design choices (KL penalty coefficient, reward model capacity) predict alignment quality — measured via both automated benchmarks and human preference studies. This requires quantitative modelling and qualitative error analysis of failure modes.
hints: This complex question needs mixed methods: automated benchmark scores for scale, human annotation for understanding failure modes.
Use stratified sampling across model scales, annotation sources, and preference dataset sizes.
Regression can model alignment score predictors; content analysis can systematically categorise reward hacking and sycophancy failure types.
